chunks: And it is narrated: When ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Ḥasan was at the point of death, his creditors gathered before him and demanded a debt owed to them. He said: “I do not have anything to give you, but be satisfied with whomever you wish from my brother and my cousin, ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn or ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar.”

The creditors said: “As for ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar, he is wealthy but delays payment. As for ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام, he is a man with no wealth, but truthful, and he is more beloved of the two to us.” So they sent to him and informed him of the matter. He, عليه السلام, said: “I guarantee the money for you until a harvest,” though he had no harvest.
The people said: “We are satisfied.” So he guaranteed it, and when the harvest came, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, provided him with wealth, and he paid it.

key_terms.أَضْمَنُ: I guarantee; I take liability for repayment
key_terms.بِدَيْنٍ: for a debt; a financial obligation owed to others
key_terms.صَدُوقٌ: truthful and trustworthy in speech and conduct
key_terms.غَلَّةٍ: harvest or yield; the expected produce or income
key_terms.غُرَمَاؤُهُ: his creditors; those to whom repayment was owed
key_terms.فَأَدَّاهُ: so he paid it in full
key_terms.ٱلْمَالَ: the wealth or funds to be repaid

ai.seo_question: How did Imam ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام respond when asked to guarantee another person’s debt?
ai.summary: This narration recounts how Imam ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام accepted responsibility for the debt of ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Ḥasan despite not possessing the means at that time. It highlights truthfulness, trustworthiness, and the fulfillment of the rights of others, while also showing reliance upon Allah عزّ وجلّ in discharging obligations.
